01a10a1e-e219-73d9-855c-cf690f3b2b25.title: Agentic CI/CD with GitHub Actions
01a10a1e-e219-73d9-855c-cf690f3b2b25.excerpt: Patterns for AI agents that interpret failures, propose fixes, and escalate with human-in-the-loop gates.
01a10a1e-e219-73d9-855c-cf690f3b2b25.body:
CI failures at 2 a.m. should not wait for a human to parse logs. **Agentic pipelines** interpret failures, propose fixes, and open draft PRs—while keeping merge gates firmly human-controlled.

## Human-in-the-loop architecture

```
fail job → agent reads logs + diff → proposes fix branch → engineer approves merge
```

Never auto-merge to main. Agents lack context on business risk, migrations, and customer commitments.

## What agents handle well

- Lint and formatter failures with deterministic fixes
- Missing lockfile updates after dependency bumps
- Flaky test triage: rerun vs quarantine recommendations
- Typo fixes in error messages surfaced by snapshot tests

## What requires escalation

- Database migration failures
- Security scanner blocks on new CVEs
- Contract test breaks across service boundaries
- Any change touching auth, payments, or PII retention

## GitHub Actions wiring

```yaml
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
jobs:
  triage:
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: node scripts/agent-triage.mjs
```

Store prompts and tool configs in-repo for reviewability. Cap token spend per run.

Agentic CI augments engineers—it does not replace judgment on production-bound changes.

## Instrumentation for agent pipelines

Log every agent suggestion with PR link, diff size, and human acceptance outcome. Monthly review: which failure classes agents resolve reliably vs which still need runbook docs. Cap concurrent agent jobs so flaky retries do not starve human CI capacity.

01a10a21-b705-70d0-992f-e96647543650.title: Product-Led Growth Playbook for 2026
01a10a21-b705-70d0-992f-e96647543650.excerpt: Self-serve onboarding, activation milestones, and in-app upgrades that compound without sales friction.
01a10a21-b705-70d0-992f-e96647543650.body:
PLG means the product **sells itself** through value experienced before sales calls—not by hiding pricing behind "contact us" forms.

## Self-serve funnel design

- Signup to value in under 10 minutes
- Progressive profiling—ask for billing only when limits hit
- In-app upgrade at moment of need (export limit, seat cap)
- Transparent pricing page linked from inside the app

## Activation milestones

Map the habit loop:

1. First success event (template used, integration connected)
2. Second session within 48 hours
3. Collaboration or data import (switching cost)
4. Paid conversion trigger tied to value metric

## Product-qualified leads

Score PQLs on usage depth, not page views:

| Signal | Weight |
|--------|--------|
| Invited teammate | High |
| Hit usage threshold | High |
| Viewed pricing | Medium |
| Read docs only | Low |

Sales engages PQLs with context: "You exported 4 reports—want SSO on the team plan?"

## Reduce sales friction

Annual plans with monthly payment option, sandbox environments, and admin controls on lower tiers for evaluators.

PLG compounds when onboarding is measurable and sales shows up with usage insight—not cold pitches.

01a10a23-b389-716c-a2eb-e5479eb081d6.title: Retainer vs Project Pricing Models
01a10a23-b389-716c-a2eb-e5479eb081d6.excerpt: When recurring revenue makes sense and how to structure hours, rollover, and scope.
01a10a23-b389-716c-a2eb-e5479eb081d6.body:
Retainers smooth revenue; projects cap risk. **Pricing model** should match work predictability and client maturity.

## Retainer fit

- Ongoing maintenance, feature slices, DevOps support
- Client needs guaranteed monthly capacity
- Relationship stable 6+ months

Structure: monthly hours bucket, rollover cap (e.g., 20% max), overage at higher rate.

## Project fit

- Defined deliverable with acceptance criteria
- New clients proving fit
- Migration or launch with fixed deadline

Fixed price with phased payments tied to milestones.

## Comparison

| Factor | Retainer | Project |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Revenue predictability | High | Lumpy |
| Scope risk | Creep risk | Bounded |
| Client commitment | Ongoing | Point-in-time |

## Hybrid

Implementation project → transition retainer for support. Document handoff criteria between phases.

Price the model that matches how work actually arrives—forcing retainers on one-off clients creates resentment both ways.

01a10a25-e1d8-71c0-911a-16db76a5980c.title: Empty State UX Patterns That Guide Users
01a10a25-e1d8-71c0-911a-16db76a5980c.excerpt: Illustrations, primary CTAs, and sample data that accelerate activation.
01a10a25-e1d8-71c0-911a-16db76a5980c.body:
Empty states are **onboarding moments**, not blank rectangles. First visit sets whether users activate or bounce confused.

## Components of strong empty states

- Illustration or icon with brand tone—not generic gray box
- Headline stating what this area is for
- Primary CTA: create first X, import, connect integration
- Secondary link to docs or template gallery

## Sample data option

For analytics dashboards, offer "load sample data" so charts demonstrate value before import friction.

## Error vs empty

Distinguish "no data yet" from "failed to load"—different copy and recovery actions.

## Checklist

| Scenario | CTA |
|----------|-----|
| Empty project list | Create project |
| Empty team | Invite teammate |
| Filtered zero results | Clear filters |

Measure activation rate from empty state CTA clicks—iterate copy like any landing page.

01a10a27-429b-76dd-9069-d255e0ece571.title: Design Ops for Growing Product Teams
01a10a27-429b-76dd-9069-d255e0ece571.excerpt: Rituals, tooling, and intake processes that keep design shipping with engineering.
01a10a27-429b-76dd-9069-d255e0ece571.body:
Design ops keeps **intake, tooling, and rituals** predictable so designers ship with engineering—not drown in slack requests and duplicate Figma files.

## Intake process

Single form: problem, success metric, deadline, eng counterpart. Triage weekly—reject vague "make it pop" requests.

## Tooling stack

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| Figma | Source of truth |
| Storybook | Component parity |
| Linear/Jira | Linked tickets |
| Loom | Async critique |

## Rituals

- Design critique weekly with cross-functional attendees
- Design-dev sync biweekly for upcoming sprint components
- Quarterly design debt sprint for doc and component cleanup

## Capacity planning

Ratio guidance: 1 designer per 6–8 engineers for complex B2B—adjust per research load.

Design ops is friction removal—measure time from request to shipped component.
